subject: New commit/best-case/pipeline rulebook + hands-on calibration sessions
messages:
From: laura_bennett@redwood.com
To: karthik_iyer@redwood.com, marissa_cole@redwood.com, vivek_kulkarni@redwood.com, Jordan Lowe <jordan.lowe@acmecorp.com>
Cc: procurement@acmecorp.com
Date: 2026-08-30T16:12:00-07:00
Subject: New commit/best-case/pipeline rulebook + hands-on calibration sessions

Team / Jordan —

Quick note and ask: we've finalized a first draft of the updated forecast "rulebook" that tightens the definitions for Commit, Best Case, and Pipeline. The goal is to reduce variance in weekly commits and make our forecast commits actionable for finance/ops while preserving healthy opportunity sequencing.

High-level changes in the attached PDF (redwood_commit_rulebook_v1.pdf):
- Commit: deals with signed commercial interest + procurement cadence confirmed; must have an agreed PO/signed SOW or clear procurement timeline within the quarter.
- Best Case: high-probability expansion/renewal scenarios that require one more stakeholder signoff and a known procurement window.
- Pipeline: early-stage opportunities where ask is exploratory or pricing is under discussion.

What I need from this group this week:
1) Internal review (karthik, marissa, vivek) — please scan the rule examples and highlight any items that will block our ability to classify deals consistently.
2) Calibration session for Acme (Jordan + procurement) — propose a 45-minute hands-on lab where we walk 6 active deals from HubSpot, apply the rulebook live, and lock in commit statuses.
3) Pre-reads for Acme finance and Redwood sales ops — attached draft slides for the lab (calibration_lab_slides_draft.pptx).

Proposed windows for the lab:
- Tue Sep 7, 10:00–10:45 PT
- Wed Sep 8, 14:00–14:45 PT
- Thu Sep 9, 09:00–09:45 PT

Jordan — would any of these work for procurement and your renewal stakeholders? If none, please propose two alternatives next week.

Thanks — I want us to run the first calibration before our next weekly forecast commit to validate the rulebook on live deals.

Best,
Laura Bennett
Director, Revenue Operations
Redwood Inference

Attachments: redwood_commit_rulebook_v1.pdf (15 pages), calibration_lab_slides_draft.pptx (12 slides)

From: karthik_iyer@redwood.com
To: laura_bennett@redwood.com, marissa_cole@redwood.com, vivek_kulkarni@redwood.com, Jordan Lowe <jordan.lowe@acmecorp.com>
Date: 2026-08-30T17:03:00-07:00
Subject: Re: New commit/best-case/pipeline rulebook + hands-on calibration sessions

Laura — thanks for sending. Quick read-through notes:
- I like the linked procurement trigger for Commit (PO/SOW). Can we add a short exception flow for "late procurement" where procurement confirms intent but PO arrives after quarter close? That will keep reps from artificially pushing to Best Case.
- Suggest adding a one-line indicator for credit approval (if finance signoff is required for the deal to be considered Commit).

Availability: Tue Sep 7 (10:00 PT) works for me. For the lab, I recommend we bring 4 deals from Acme with different risk profiles and 2 internal demo deals so the team sees edge cases.

Karthik
Senior Revenue Operations Manager

Laura — thanks for the clear write-up and the PDF. Procurement is generally aligned with having a short checklist to mark a deal as "commit". The proposed windows look fine.

A couple of notes from our side:
- For Acme, PO timing is often the blocker — if procurement can verbally commit to a quarter but PO arrives later, we still need to account for that in our internal forecast. Would the exception flow Karthik suggested be documented so we can use it consistently?
- We also want a short explanation we can share with our finance team that explains why a "Commit" is being counted in the quarter despite a PO lag (i.e., criteria that finance can rely on).

We can do Tue Sep 7, 10:00 PT. I will invite our finance and procurement leads.

Jordan Lowe
Head of Partnerships, Acme Corp
